---
title: "select() does not keep the same column twice"
ref: TDY-04
categories: [tidyverse]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'names(select(mtcars, foo = mpg, mpg))'
reponse: '"foo"'
attendu: "`\"foo\" \"mpg\"`"
versions: "All versions of {dplyr}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2024)"
---

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

cars <- head(mtcars, n = 2)
select(cars, foo = mpg, mpg)
```
:::

## Why

`select()` picks columns, it does not copy them. `foo = mpg` selects `mpg` while renaming it, and the second mention of `mpg` refers to the same column, already taken: it is not duplicated. Only one column is left, under the first name given, without a warning.

## The fix

To get a copy, create it with `mutate()`, then select.

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

cars |>
  mutate(foo = mpg) |>
  select(foo, mpg)
```
:::
